name: java-httpserver-api
title: Java HTTP API
blurb: Java 21 JSON service on the JDK's own com.sun.net.httpserver: pure counting and contract classes, a hand-written JSON reader that keeps a string apart from a number, and a Makefile over javac with -Xlint:all -Werror
default_description: A Java 21 JSON service on the JDK HTTP server.

verify.name: http
verify.cmd:
set -e
if curl -fsS --max-time 2 http://127.0.0.1:5442/health >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo 'port 5442 is already answering - stop that process before running this step'
  exit 1
fi
PORT=5442 java -cp build/classes {{ package_name }}.App > .java-http.log 2>&1 &
server=$!
trap 'kill -TERM -"$server" 2>/dev/null || kill $server 2>/dev/null || true; wait $server 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
i=0
while [ $i -lt 120 ]; do
  if curl -fsS --max-time 2 http://127.0.0.1:5442/health >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    break
  fi
  i=$((i + 1))
  sleep 0.25
done
if [ $i -ge 120 ]; then
  cat .java-http.log
  echo 'the server did not answer in time'
  exit 1
fi
kill -0 $server 2>/dev/null || { cat .java-http.log; echo 'the server exited before it answered'; exit 1; }
health=$(curl -sS --max-time 10 http://127.0.0.1:5442/health)
test "$health" = '{"status":"ok"}'
get=$(curl -sS --max-time 10 'http://127.0.0.1:5442/stats?text=hello%20world%0A')
printf '%s' "$get" | grep -q '"lines":1'
printf '%s' "$get" | grep -q '"bytes":12'
posted=$(curl -sS --max-time 10 -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary '{"text":"a b\nc\n"}' http://127.0.0.1:5442/stats)
printf '%s' "$posted" | grep -q '"words":3'
missing=$(curl -sS --max-time 10 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:5442/stats)
test "$missing" = 422
broken=$(curl -sS --max-time 10 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary 'nope' http://127.0.0.1:5442/stats)
test "$broken" = 422
number=$(curl -sS --max-time 10 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary '{"text":42}' http://127.0.0.1:5442/stats)
test "$number" = 422
gone=$(curl -sS --max-time 10 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:5442/nope)
test "$gone" = 404
wrong=$(curl -sS --max-time 10 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:5442/health)
test "$wrong" = 405
